ops.body:
cc-sync lanes launched.

cc-sync architecture contract: cc-notes doc f078f23. Coordinator decisions in it:
- The capture unit is the worktree, holding all of its sessions. A checkpoint is one root group Ref over a code manifest, the Orca descriptor and the session manifests.
- The only WatchDir is cc-sync's own stamp root. The scheduler runs a 30 s metadata scan; no Claude hooks are installed and user Claude settings are not modified.
- The CLI reads the store read-only after pinning through the helper.
- Every session in a checkpoint is installed natively at pickup, so dormant bindings are resumable. Only the selected sessions are resumed.

Additions to running contracts:
- Orca a8da144 adds crossMachineRecovery.activity (`orca recovery activity --json`) for the human-focus tier.
- synckit 6c3cec2 adds artifact.OpenReadOnly for the pickup CLI.

Stage A Run wf_62b1c2a2-300 has five parallel lanes, each with its own worktree under /Users/yasyf/.claude/worktrees/cc-sync/<lane> (branches cc-sync/<lane>):
- native-fixtures: empirical Claude resume semantics on the installed 2.1.283, where the system-prompt snapshot lives and how relocation works; a fixture corpus plus a native-tagged harness.
- claudenative: Jx UTF-16 encoding with the hash suffix, liveness, incremental scan.
- scheduler: 2m/5m/15m/1h tiers, 2 workers, at most 1 capture per repo.
- orcabridge: local-only orca CLI adapter.
- cli: exact picker JSON and exit codes.

Stage B (catalog/consumer/sessionarchive/codesnap/capture/resident/pickup/sessionrestore + e2e) launches once the synckit and reposync foundations and the native findings land.
